title: Aru — recorded forms and moments
scope: Six selected visual moments from the story, not a complete lifespan, fixed biological ages, power levels, or a progression across eras. The account opens in Era −1; the later nursery return is not assigned an invented date.
artNotice: The events and stated appearance changes are sourced. Exact shapes, most colors, poses and proportions are new visual interpretations, not newly discovered lore.

stages.title: The undecided newborn
stages.summary: Aru first appears as a small floating, vaguely person-shaped figure. Its head and limbs redraw themselves, its surface shifts between translucence, shadow and pale skinlike appearance, and it initially has no face.
stages.quote: The figure was vaguely person-shaped, though its edges redrew themselves every few moments.
stages.artNote: The pale lavender palette and the precise silhouette are illustration choices; the source describes changing appearance, not a fixed design.

stages.title: Discovering dispersal
stages.summary: During laughter, Aru loses cohesion and disperses into bright fragments. Iri restores the form; two newly rendered eyes appear. This is an early reversible discovery, not evidence of the later degraded chapel concept.
stages.quote: The child made the sound until its entire body lost cohesion and collapsed into a cloud of bright fragments.
stages.artNote: This image depicts the moment of dispersal. Fragment shape, arrangement and color are illustration choices.

stages.title: The repair Aru chose to keep
stages.summary: A fall fragments one shoulder. Aru pulls the pieces back unevenly and refuses Iri’s correction. One arm remains darker for thirty-two cycles.
stages.quote: One arm remained darker than the other.
stages.artNote: The story does not specify which arm or its hue. The side, violet shade and small eye details in this drawing are illustration choices.

stages.title: Angular and colorless
stages.summary: When Iri returns from the Council review, the nursery has become a maze of repeated rooms. Aru’s body is angular and colorless. This is a described state in that scene, not an age or permanent evolution.
stages.quote: Its body had become angular and colorless.
stages.artNote: The grayscale follows the source. The crouched posture, facets and exact proportions are illustration choices.

stages.title: The imposed complete form
stages.summary: A ring of structured light surrounds Aru. The intervention fixes the limbs into approved proportions, corrects the dark arm, closes the unfinished edges and makes the eyes symmetrical. Iri and Aru interrupt it. This is imposed stabilization, not Aru’s chosen mature or ideal form.
stages.quote: For the first time, Aru looked complete.
stages.artNote: The single restraint ring visualizes the intervention described at stories-p02448. Its geometry and color are illustration choices; it is not the later concept’s decorative pair of rings.

stages.title: Surfaces around a warm light
stages.summary: Long after the naming assembly and hearings, Aru returns to the nursery after many changes of embodiment. On that day it has no humanlike face: loose surfaces orbit a warm central light. Aru extends a surface into unfinished space, then steps forward while Iri follows.
stages.quote: Its body was a loose arrangement of surfaces orbiting a warm central light.
stages.artNote: The source establishes loose orbiting surfaces and a warm center, but not their count, palette or arrangement. This is the latest described appearance in this story, not a final identity.

laterConcept.title: Undated possible later winged-galaxy form
laterConcept.status: Separate concept · story not yet written
laterConcept.note: The first spark, eight wings, paired decorative rings and galaxy backdrop belong to the earlier artistic sequence. They are not established stages in The First Newborn. The winged form may be explored later; neither its date nor its place in Aru’s life is confirmed. The degraded chapel animation is also a separate visual concept, not a recorded ending.
